The central-lift order calculation uses M-mu I invertible. The complete matrix rank-one enumeration and actual group-element checks in check_prime_cyclotomic.py agree with the predicted counts for p=5,7,11,13,29. The calculations are finite checks and the general claim relies on the explicit proof.

originality.rationale: Full primary literature comparison shows that the 2026 Frobenius paper addresses group properties but not extraspecial prime-complement counting, the 2019 Kumar-Pradhan paper supplies unrestricted automorphism normal forms but not fixed-point-free prime-order spectra, and Wall addresses semisimple conjugacy in ordinary symplectic groups rather than the extra-special central lifts. The compared Heisenberg group twisted-conjugacy census aggregates automorphism orders. Closest published results found by actual published-finding corpus and web searches do not state or directly imply the complete displayed all-rank formula without new restrictions and orbit calculations. Historical priority remains qualified by possible older semisimple conjugacy specializations.
residual_risks: Historical priority may be implicit in unindexed specialist Frobenius-kernel classifications or conjugacy tables for finite general symplectic similitude groups; no stronger exact covering source was found in the inspected materials.
A fully systematic audit of every historical pre-2026 thesis and original classical group treatise has not been completed.

value.rationale: The parameter space p,n,ell and both natural extraspecial isomorphism types is motivated by prime-order complements in split Frobenius groups. A closed all-rank count, full conjugacy-type spectrum, and exponent-type obstruction go materially beyond checking one exceptional group or one arbitrary rank. The count permits enumeration and classification of nonabelian Frobenius semidirect actions and is not a substitution into a displayed known table. It has clear group-theoretic interpretability even without a claimed downstream theorem.
